chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Husayn ibn Mukhtar, from Al-Walid ibn Sabih, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

I accompanied him between Mecca and Medina. A beggar came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then another came, so he ordered that he be given. Then the fourth came, so Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'May Allah satisfy you.'
Then he turned to us and said: 'Indeed, we have what we can give him, but I fear that we may become like one of the three whose supplication is not answered.'
A man whom Allah gave wealth, so he spent it in that which was not its rightful place, then he says: 'O Allah, grant me,' so it is not answered for him.
And a man who supplicates against his wife that he be freed from her, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made her matter to him.
And a man who supplicates against his neighbor, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the way open for him to move away from his neighbor's vicinity and sell his house.

key_terms.أَنْفَقَهُ فِي غَيْرِ حَقِّهِ: He spent it in that which was not its rightful place
key_terms.يُشْبِعُكَ اللَّهُ: May Allah satisfy you (a specific supplication)

ai.seo_question: What are the three types of people whose supplication is not answered according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) illustrates the principle of *hikmah* (wisdom) in charity by withholding from a fourth beggar, fearing that indiscriminate giving might lead to the supplicant becoming one of the three whose prayers are rejected. This hadith highlights that the efficacy of dua is contingent not only on sincerity but also on the recipient's conduct, specifically regarding the misuse of wealth, marital patience, and neighborly relations.
